{{pagebanner|Condesa and Roma Wikivoyage banner.jpg|pgname=Condesa and Roma}}
The '''Condesa''' and '''Roma''' district of [[Mexico City]] is a residential and restaurant area on both sides of Insurgentes avenue (Condesa on the west side, Roma on the east side) between Viaducto Miguel Alemán in the south and Avenida Chapultepec in the north. It's a large area developed in the 1930s-1950s with mostly [[art deco architecture]], large parks, and a relaxed atmosphere. The area is popular with an eclectic artsy crowd who stay in the many small bed and breakfast inns and some of the city's most cutting edge [[Contemporary art]] galleries.

==Understand==
La Condesa consists of several colonias on the west side of Avenida Insurgentes. It was an extremely fashionable part of Mexico City during the Golden Age of Mexican cinema in the 1940s and 1950s when it was home to many film stars. Mexico City's first Bauhaus-type apartment building, the Edificio Basurto, was built in 1938 and was popular amongst entertainment industry figures. The 1985 earthquake hit the area hard, and many of the art deco and midcentury buildings were abandoned as residents moved to areas like [[Mexico City/Polanco|Polanco]] and [[Mexico City/Chapultepec|Lomas de Chapultepec]]. Due to the high availability of housing stock and fascinating architecture, the area was rediscovered by artists, musicians and other creative people in the mid-1990s, resulting an abundance of hip restaurants, cafes, and bars. Some of the pioneers have moved on to neighboring areas as rents increased, but the building boom has continued the neighborhood's tradition of exceptional architecture.

Roma, on the opposite side of Insurgentes, has less greenery and is more urbanized, but has a similar flavor. Although it was developed at the same time as Condesa, it was more middle-class, with a large number of European immigrants who had fled the Spanish Civil War and the Holocaust, and despite the damage of the 1985 earthquake kept this character into the 2000s. It is going through a period of very fast real estate development, as prices and popularity are increasing. There are new bars and restaurants popping up every week, and it's well worth a visit.

===Orientation===
Condesa is focused around '''Avenida Amsterdam''', a large, oval street that used to be the track of the area's horse racetrack (thus the name for this colonia, ''Hipódromo Condesa''). Av. Amsterdam is long and slightly curving, making it easy to lose your direction while going along it. It's dotted with small roundabouts where other streets cross it, and a large part of the area inside it is taken up by the Parque México, with an open-air amphitheatre on one end, and small lanes amongst large trees and fountains on the other. There are several good restaurants and bars in this area, but it's the most residential, and least urban, of the Condesa.

The other part of Condesa is Col. Condesa, a bit further away from Insurgentes, on the west side of Av. Nuevo León. This is much more heavily developed, and has an impressive assortment of bars, restaurants, and sidewalk cafes.

Roma consists of two colonias: '''Roma Norte''' (''North'') and '''Roma Sur''' (''South''), divided by Coahuila street. Roma Norte is the most hip, while Roma Sur is quieter.

==Get in==
{{Mapframe|19.4151|-99.1483|zoom=13}}
{{mapshapes|Q735042}}
===By metro===

Condesa and Roma don't have Metro stations directly inside the area, but there are a few stations at its periphery that will get you within a short walk of your destination.

For Condesa, Metro stations '''Insurgentes''', '''Sevilla''', '''Chapultepec''' and '''Juanacatlan''' on Line 1 border along the north and west side of the area, and stations '''Patriotismo''' and '''Chilpancingo''' on Line 9 border the south.

For Roma, stations '''Insurgentes''' and '''Cuahtemoc''' on Line 1 border the north, and stations '''Ninos Heroes''', '''Hospital General''' and '''Centro Medico''' on Line 3 border the east.

===By metrobus===

The Metrobús, which runs up and down Avenida Insurgentes, is a very convenient way of getting to Condesa and Roma.

Line 1 travels along Av. Insurgentes (the division between Condesa and Roma). Stops serving this area are Insurgentes, Alvaro Obregon, Sonora, and Campeche.

==Get around==
[[File:Corredor Cultural Álvaro Obregón, Ciudad de México (32143559953).jpg|thumb|Ecobici station in Roma on Av Alvaro Obregon]]
Condesa and Roma are very walkable, though some streets in Roma are poorly lit and a cautious traveler might avoid walking smaller streets at night.

Taxis are available everywhere. The white taxis with magenta roofs are generally safe, but for added security, have hotel or restaurant staff call a radio taxi for you. Uber and other rideshare applications work extremely well in Mexico City.

===By bike===
Bicycling is increasingly popular in Mexico City where the city government establishes bike lanes in several downtown areas. Many Mexico City thoroughfares are too crowded to safely ride a bike, but Condesa and Roma have some wonderful neighborhood streets with lighter traffic where a bike can be safely ridden.

The CDMX city government sponsors a bike loaner program called '''[https://ecobici.cdmx.gob.mx/ Ecobici]''', which includes more than 400 stations around the city where you can rent a bike, or return one that you picked up elsewhere. There are more than two dozen Ecobici stations scattered throughout Condesa and in both Roma Norte and Roma Sur.

Dedicated bike lanes (''ciclovias'') run along Avenida Insurgentes, a major thoroughfare from Churrubusco to the [[Mexico City/Centro|Centro Historico]]. The bike lanes are physically separated from traffic lanes with low concrete barriers. However, given the extremely heavy congestion on this road, cyclists must be constantly alert for obstacles, incursions into bike lanes, and aggressive drivers at intersections. A secure bike storage facility (called a ''Bicipuerto'') is near the Glorieta de Los Insurgentes, where you can lock up your bike and take a Metro train to other parts of the city. ''See also [[Cycling in Mexico City]].''

* {{see
| name=Casa Museo Leonora Carrington | alt= | url=https://casaleonoracarrington.uam.mx/ | email=
| address=Chihuahua 194, Roma Norte | lat=19.416974 | long=-99.162932 | directions=
| phone= | tollfree=
| hours=temporarily closed | price=
| lastedit=2023-05-27
| content=Home and studio of surrealist feminist artist Leonora Carrington. Born in Britain, Carrington lived in this Mexico City home for 60 years -- almost all of her artistically prolific career. Carrington is difficult to classify. She worked in Mexico, but was educated and raised in Great Britain, so she had none of the sense of "Mexicanidad" (Mexican identity) that permeates most modern art in Mexico. She was a surrealist and her work is best understood in an international context though she was readily accepted into the Mexican artistic community. A fascinating person and an immense talent.
}}

==Buy==

There are many small shops around Condesa, selling clothing from independent designers, crafts and trendy stuff. This place recalls the Palermo neighborhood in Buenos Aires or SOHO in New York. In Roma, trendy shops are interspersed with ice cream shops and bookstores along Av. Alvaro Obregon. A block away, Calle Colima has a number of trendy cutting-edge boutiques. 

Roma also has two small malls, one by Insurgentes, the Plaza Insurgentes, and another on the east side of the area, by Avenida Cuauhtémoc, the Plaza Cuauhtémoc. Both have stores and Cinemex movie theaters.

==Eat==
In addition to a lively restaurant scene, the area has some of the best street food in Mexico City.

===Street food===
Vendors usually concentrate along Avenida Insurgentes which runs between the neighborhoods, particularly next to major metro stations.

The intersection of Av Insurgentes and Av Alvaro Obregon has a concentration of some of the city's favorite sidewalk taco stands. The intersection is widely known as a place to go if your stomach starts rumbling at 3am because the taco stands keep the grills sizzling all night long.

===Condesa===
[[File:FuenteDeLasCibelesP2v2.jpg|thumb|A number of restaurants and pubs are around the Fuente de las Cibeles, one of Roma's most popular parks]]
Condesa has a developed restaurant scene, centered on a few blocks surrounding the triple-street intersection of Michoacán, Atlixco and Vincente Suárez, which can be pretty crowded during the day and very popular at night, especially on weekends. The restaurant area extends all along Michoacán from Tamaulipas to Mazatlan. You will find the majority of the restaurants listed below in this area.

The restaurant is not a "vegan" restaurant, but they heavily emphasize vegetarian dishes using locally sourced produce grown in the chinampas of Xochimilco. The restaurant claims to have achieved zero waste in their operations.
}}
* {{eat

===Roma===
Roma has historically had a smaller restaurant scene than Condesa, but this has been changing in the late 2010s and early 2020s, with a few restaurants moving to Roma and a few opening second locations there. Today, there are many places to eat without traveling to other parts of the city. A few are listed here, but you will also be able to discover many others on your own.

*{{eat
| name=El Califa | url= | email=
| address=Av. Alvaro Obregon 174, Roma Nte. | lat=19.417697872107155 | long=-99.16258501824264 | directions=a block or two from Av. Nuevo León
| phone= | tollfree= | fax=
| hours=Sun-Wed 13:00-23:00, Thu-Sat 13:00-05:00 | price=M$100-200
| content=Popular taco chain with various locations in Mexico City. A little overpriced, but very high quality tacos. The specialty is the ''gaonera'' (try the one with cheese), a large, thin slice of tender beef, roasted and placed on a tortilla. The house salsas are also notable for being made with fried tomatoes. After dinner, try the traditional Mexican coffee with cinnamon, ''café de olla''.
}}
*{{eat
| name=BB Kfe | alt= | url= | email=
| address=Tlaxcala 69, Col. Roma | lat=19.408291 | long=-99.163929 | directions=between Campeche and Coahuila, one block east of Insurgentes Sur
| phone=+52 55 5219 7381 | tollfree=
| hours=Mon-Fri 11:00-22:00, Sat 11:00-20:00, closed Sun | price=M$40-60
| lastedit=2025-05-28
| content=This small cafe offers excellent food at very low prices until 18:00. A set dinner includes a soup, a salad, a main dish, a small dessert, fruit flavored water, and coffee. The pasta dishes are good and portions are abundant.
}}
* {{eat
| name=Mog | alt= | url= | email=
| address=Obregon 40, Roma Nte. | lat=19.416512273658068 | long=-99.15506100475096
| phone=+52 55 5264 1629
| hours=Daily 13:00 - 00:00
| lastedit=2024-03-02
| content=Tasty authentic Japanese food at good prices in a very warm, randomly decorated place. A nice spot to hang out and have a drink or coffee/tea also. Impressive tea selection.
}}
* {{eat | name=Las Flautas | alt= | url=http://www.las-flautas.com/sucursales/tonala/ | email=contacto@las-flautas.com | address=Tonalá 130 | lat=19.41573 | long=-99.16189 | directions=Cuauhtemoc | phone=+52 55 5584 0369 | tollfree= | fax= | image=Las Flautas Colonia Roma.jpg | hours=Daily 09:00-22:00 | price=M$80-100 | content=Serves very good flautas and tacos de guisado. Delivery available.
}} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}
* {{eat

==Drink==
[[File:Advertising on the side of buildings, col. Condesa Hipódromo, Condesa, Mexico City.jpg|thumbnail|Advertising on the side of buildings, col. Condesa Hipódromo]]
In Condesa, you will find a number of bars on the north end of Avenida Tamaulipas, in addition to the restaurant area mentioned above.

===Condesa===
* {{drink
| name=Salon Malafama | alt= | url=https://salonmalafama.com/ | email=
| address=Av Michoacán 78, Colonia Condesa | lat=19.411585 | long=-99.173708 | directions=
| phone=+52 55 5553 5138 | tollfree=
| hours=Sun-Wed 13:00 - 01:00, Thu-Sat 13:00 - 03:00 | price=
| lastedit=2024-02-09
| content=Trendy pool hall with a dozen billiards tables, cold beers, mezcal cocktails and a menu of burgers, fries, tacos and other light fare.
}}

* {{drink
| name=La Clandestina | alt= | url=https://laclandestina.mx/ | email=
| address=Alvaro Obregon 298, Condesa | lat=19.416461 | long=-99.169214 | directions=
| phone=+52 55 5525 1100 | tollfree=
| hours=Mon-Tue 18:30 - 01:00, Wed-Sat 18:30 - 02:00, closed Sun | price=
| lastedit=2024-03-02
| content=Dark, intimate mezcal bar with an extensive range of artesanal mezcals and their own house brand, ''Enmascarado'', which is available in bottles to go. A well-curated mezcal list explains a bit about the origins, manufacture, and sensory highlights of different mezcals. Excellent place to experiment with a sampler and learn a bit about the spirit.
}}

* {{drink
| name=GinGin | url=http://www.gingin.mx/
| address=Av. Oaxaca 87 | lat=19.419825203848426 | long=-99.16746991551258
| phone=+52 551 484 9194
| hours=Daily 16:00 - 03:00 | price=
| lastedit=2025-01-29
| content=Popular cocktail lounge with upscale atmosphere and creative cocktails. Reservations are a necessity and the place has a reputation for "losing" reservations, and overcharging (so check the bill carefully).
}}
* {{drink
| name=Lagerbar Hercules | alt= | url= | email=
| address=Campeche 322, Hipódromo | lat=19.408849 | long=-99.172774 | directions=
| phone=+52 555 286 9334 | tollfree=
| hours=Mon-Sat 13ː00 - 23ː30, Sun 13ː00 - 20ː00 | price=
| lastedit=2026-02-02
| content=Taproom for a Queretaro-based craft brewery specializing in an eclectic collection of predominantly European style lager beers. The most unusual is probably the Rye Lager. They also have a nice Schwarzbier, seasonal brews like Oktoberfest, and a Mexican Lager intended to emulate a Corona or Tecate. Good selection of bar bites and the crowd is an eclectic mix of young professionals, ex-pats and digital nomads.
}}

===Roma===
[[File:Casa franca roma.jpg|thumb|Live jazz bands perform at Casa Franca in Roma]]
*{{drink
| name=Mama Rumba | alt= | url= | email=
| address=Av. Medellin, Col. Roma | lat=19.413982 | long=-99.164930 | directions=one block from Insurgentes
| phone=+52 55 5264 7823 | tollfree=
| hours=Thu-Sat 18:00-03:00 | price=
| lastedit=2024-02-09
| content=One of the most popular [[Salsa dancing in Latin America|dance clubs/bars]] in the city, usually very full, plays salsa, merengue, and other Cuban music. There is another branch in San Angel, which is more popular with the younger crowd and can sometimes be hard to get into. Come early and get a free salsa lesson.
}}

* {{drink
| name=Licoreria Limantour | alt= | url=http://limantour.tv/ | email=
| address=Av. Álvaro Obregón 106, Roma Nte | lat=19.418276 | long=-99.159345 | directions=
| phone=+52 55 5264 4122 | tollfree=
| hours=Sun-Thu 18:00 - 00:00, Fri-Sat 15:00 - 02:00 | price=M$500
| lastedit=2024-02-09
| content=Claims to be "one of the world's top 50 bars", which seems rather dubious to me, but the cocktails ''are'' amazingly good! They have a wide assortment of spirits behind the bar with a mind-boggling selection of tequilas and mezcals. Upscale place with correspondingly upscale prices. Elegant atmosphere.
}}

* {{drink
| name=Tlecan | alt= | url= | email=
| address=Alvaro Obregon 228, Roma Nte | lat=19.417131 | long=-99.165462 | directions=at intersection with Av. Insurgentes
| phone=+52 55 1334 4745 | tollfree=
| hours=Daily 18:00 - 02:00 | price=
| lastedit=2024-03-02
| content=Small, intimate mescaleria that is just a few blocks from La Clandestina, with a similar focus and clientele, but a smaller, but exceptionally well focused mezcal list. Waiters are very knowledgable and can explain the types of maguey used by a particular brand and how it expresses itselfe in appearance, aroma, and flavor. In addition to outstanding artesanal mezcals from Oaxaca, they have a few bottles of mezcal sub-styles, such as ''bacanora'' (usually found only in Sonora) and ''raicilla'' (usually found only in Jalisco). A good bar for the curious epicure to learn about mezcal.
}}

* {{drink
| name=Jazzatlan Capital | alt= | url=https://www.jazzatlan.club/capital | email=
| address=Guanajuato 239, Roma Nte | lat=19.416131 | long=-99.164850 | directions=at intersection with Av. Insurgentes
| phone=+52 55 6131 1119 | tollfree=
| hours=Daily 18:00 - 02:00 | price=Cover M$400
| lastedit=2024-03-02
| content=Laid back club with a sort of retro-hipster vibe. The club is an offshoot of a popular club founded in Cholula. Features live jazz music nightly with an upstairs club (reservations required, can be made via Whatsapp) and a downstairs salon that becomes standing room only when a good band is in the house.
}}

* {{drink
| name=Janis | alt= | url=https://janisroma.club/
| address=Calle Queretaro , Roma Nte | lat=19.414428795246216 | long=-99.1641483041453
| phone=+52 55 2176 6710 
| hours=Wed-Sat 23:00 - 05:00, closed Sun-Tue | price=M$1000
| lastedit=2025-01-29
| content=Popular rock-oriented club named in tribute to Janis Joplin. Lively crowd, large drinks. Be aware they add a 20% tip on all bills.
}}

* {{drink
| name=Mano Santa Mezcal | alt= | url=
| address=Av. Insurgentes Sur 219, Roma Nte.  | lat=19.41994928301838 | long=-99.16446509250474
| phone=+52 55 3662 6088
| hours=Mon-Wed 18:00 - 02:00, Thu-Sun 15:00 - 02:00  | price=M$200
| lastedit=2025-01-29
| content=Hip contemporary bar specializing in mezcals with a wide variety of brands, many with very distinct flavor profiles. Many mezcal cocktails are offered including the classic mezcalhina, with a citric tang to it. Light bar snacks are available including a wonderful guacamole with chapulines (grasshoppers). A selection of local craft beers are available. English speaking staff available. Credit cards accepted.

* {{drink
| name=Casa Franca | alt= | url= | email=
| address=Merida 109, Roma Norte | lat=19.419199 | long=-99.157517 | directions=
| phone=+52 55 5208 2265 | tollfree=

* {{drink

* {{drink
| name=Club San Luis | alt= | url= | email=

| phone=+52 555 574 2639 | tollfree=

==Connect==
Mexico City has excellent 5G coverage everywhere, including all parts of Condesa and Roma. Hotels and restaurants all have high-speed internet, most with free WiFi.
